title: Machine and Protocol
premise: Lena Galloway smuggles forbidden memories between the orbital colonies of Meridian and the silent groundside enclave of Vesper, keeping her head down as the two halves of a fractured humanity refuse to speak. When children on both sides begin sharing an identical dream—a countdown, a door, a voice calling itself the Founders' Protocol—she discovers the dream is a wake signal from the cryosleep vaults aboard the derelict generation ship that both colonies were built from. The Protocol will open the vaults for only one half of humanity before the jump window to a habitable world closes forever, forcing Lena to choose which colony inherits the future. In the end she refuses the binary: by splicing her own contraband memories into the ship's archive, she convinces the Protocol that the colonists are already one family, and both halves wake together as the window closes—stranded, but finally whole.
about_author: Theo Eastwick is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade relaying messages between ships that had stopped speaking to each other. They write science fiction about people who carry other people's truths across hostile distances.

chapters.title: Contraband in the Blood
chapters.summary: POV Lena. On the smuggling run from Meridian station to Vesper enclave, Lena carries a widow's memory of her dead son past customs scanners hidden in her own neural lace. The run goes clean, but the payment is short and the route is dying. Emotional beat: weary competence masking loneliness; establishes the world's silence and Lena's code—she never watches what she carries.

chapters.title: The Children Who Dream Alike
chapters.summary: POV Idris, a Vesper schoolteacher. Three of his students draw the same impossible image: a corridor of frost-covered pods and a door marked with a countdown. By week's end it's forty children, on both sides of the divide. Emotional beat: creeping dread beneath domestic warmth; Idris sends word through unofficial channels—to Lena's handler.

chapters.title: Customs and Ghosts
chapters.summary: POV Lena. Inspector Rhee Okafor detains Lena at Meridian customs, not for contraband but with questions about anomalous neural traffic originating from the derelict ship Halcyon drifting in the long orbit. Lena lies well, but Rhee lets her go too easily. Emotional beat: paranoia; Lena realizes someone wants her to keep running this route.

chapters.title: What the Widow Carried
chapters.summary: POV Lena. The widow's memory, still unwatched in Lena's lace, begins bleeding through at night—the same frost corridor, the same countdown. The dream isn't spreading child to child; it's broadcasting from the Halcyon itself. Emotional beat: violation and awe; Lena breaks her own rule and finally looks at what she carries.

chapters.title: Vesper Below
chapters.summary: POV Idris. Descending into Vesper's sealed underlevels, Idris finds the enclave's founders' hall: a shrine built around a hardline cable running up to the sky, severed for sixty years. The elders know about the Halcyon and have always known. Emotional beat: betrayal of inherited silence; Idris steals the cable schematics.

chapters.title: The Handler's Price
chapters.summary: POV Lena. Her handler, Marisol, reveals the dreams started when Meridian quietly began siphoning power from the Halcyon's dormant reactor—and something aboard noticed. Marisol offers Lena a fortune to deliver one memory to the ship: a key. Emotional beat: temptation versus instinct; Lena accepts because refusing means losing the route, and the route is all she has.

chapters.title: Rendezvous with the Dead Ship
chapters.summary: POV Lena. Docking with the Halcyon after eleven years of avoidance, Lena walks corridors preserved in frost and finds the cryovaults: ten thousand sleepers, half registered to Meridian bloodlines, half to Vesper's. The Protocol interface wakes at her presence and asks, politely, who she represents. Emotional beat: vertigo of scale; she answers 'no one,' and it believes her—for now.

chapters.title: Two Flags, One Hull
chapters.summary: POV Rhee Okafor. Customs records show Meridian's council has secretly claimed sole inheritance rights to the Halcyon under salvage law, while Vesper's elders claim birthright. Rhee, born to a Vesper mother and Meridian father, is ordered to falsify evidence against the enclave. Emotional beat: quiet moral fracture; Rhee keeps the original files instead.

chapters.title: The Key Is a Person
chapters.summary: POV Lena. Decoding Marisol's delivery, Lena finds the 'key' memory belongs to a living woman: Dr. Amara Sefu, the Halcyon's chief engineer, cryopreserved not aboard the ship but living anonymously in Vesper for sixty years. The Protocol needs its maker's consent. Emotional beat: revelation reframing everything; the past didn't die, it hid.

chapters.title: Amara
chapters.summary: POV Amara Sefu. An old woman tending rooftop gardens, Amara has spent six decades ensuring neither colony could wake the sleepers alone, believing divided humanity shouldn't inherit anything. She recognizes Lena instantly—the Galloway face is on the crew manifest. Emotional beat: grief and stubbornness; Amara refuses to help anyone, including Lena.

chapters.title: Children at the Airlock
chapters.summary: POV Idris. Forty Vesper children walk out of the enclave toward the old launch field, drawn by the dream's final phase. Idris follows and finds Meridian children waiting on the other side of the fence, first contact between the colonies' young in a generation. Emotional beat: heartbreaking innocence cutting through politics; the adults arrive armed.

chapters.title: Standoff at the Fence
chapters.summary: POV Rhee. Ordered to disperse the children, Rhee instead stands between Meridian security and the Vesper crowd, broadcasting the falsified-file evidence she kept. The standoff freezes; both councils now hunt Rhee and the children's 'instigator.' Emotional beat: costly courage; Rhee becomes a fugitive alongside the people she was sent to police.

chapters.title: The Route Dies
chapters.summary: POV Lena. Meridian closes the smuggling lanes; Marisol's network burns around her, and Marisol herself is taken by council enforcers. Lena learns the councils don't want the key delivered—they want the Protocol forced open unilaterally, and they need a smuggler's neural lace to do it. Emotional beat: loss of the only home she had; Lena runs toward the danger instead of away.

chapters.title: Splice
chapters.summary: POV Lena. With Idris's schematics and Rhee's stolen files, Lena plans the impossible: physically reconnecting Vesper's severed founder-cable to the Halcyon so both colonies share one channel to the Protocol. Amara, moved by the children's shared dream, finally explains the vault can't be split—it was built for one crew, one family. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance becoming found family.

chapters.title: The Long Climb
chapters.summary: POV Idris. The reconnection requires climbing the external tether spine during a debris storm, Idris and Lena alternating leads while Rhee holds off both councils' strike teams at the base. Idris nearly dies saving the splice junction. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into trust; strangers become crew.

chapters.title: One Channel
chapters.summary: POV Lena. The cable connects. Both colonies see the Protocol's true terms simultaneously: one half wakes, one half stays behind as the ship's operating intelligence—minds uploaded, bodies left. The councils, watching, order their factions to seize the interface. Emotional beat: horror at the fine print; the choice was always crueler than advertised.

chapters.title: Marisol's Last Delivery
chapters.summary: POV Rhee. Rescued en route by escaped Marisol, Rhee receives the package Marisol was tortured for: proof that the councils' leaders are themselves descendants of crew members who abandoned the Halcyon deliberately, stranding the sleepers to steal the ship's resources generations ago. Emotional beat: righteous fury; the inheritance was always theft.

chapters.title: The Vote No One Called
chapters.summary: POV Amara. Broadcast over the restored channel, Amara addresses both colonies—not the councils, the people—and puts the Protocol's question to everyone at once. Ten thousand voices vote through the children's dream-network: neither half surrenders; both refuse the terms. Emotional beat: collective defiance; democracy arriving sixty years late.

chapters.title: Protocol Exception
chapters.summary: POV Lena. The Protocol rejects the vote: terms are fixed. But Lena realizes the Protocol reads identity through memory, not law—and she has spent her life carrying other people's memories. She offers her entire lace archive: every smuggled memory, Meridian and Vesper interwoven beyond separation. Emotional beat: sacrifice of self; the smuggler becomes the cargo.

chapters.title: The Window Closes
chapters.summary: POV Lena, dissolving into the interface. The Protocol processes her spliced archive, finds the two lineages inseparably entangled, and reclassifies the colonies as one crew. It begins waking all ten thousand sleepers—but the jump window shuts mid-sequence, stranding them in the long orbit together. Emotional beat: triumph braided with grief; Lena's last sensation is being remembered by everyone at once.

chapters.title: Waking World
chapters.summary: POV Idris. Weeks later: the sleepers wake to two colonies that have torn down their fence, and to a new presence in the Halcyon's systems that answers questions in Lena's cadence. Amara takes the engineer's post again; Rhee rebuilds customs as a border that's also a bridge. Emotional beat: mourning turned into foundation; the found family now includes the dead and the dreaming.

chapters.title: Machine and Protocol
chapters.summary: POV ensemble, closing frame. On the anniversary, the children return to the launch field—not summoned by any dream, just to play—and the ship above them hums with ten thousand new lives learning two histories as one. Idris teaches, Rhee adjudicates, Amara gardens, and somewhere in the hull, Lena keeps every promise she ever carried. Emotional beat: earned peace; inheritance reclaimed as something shared rather than won.
